_comment: SECURITY DEFINER functions that a browser role may execute, that write, and that do not consult auth.uid()/auth.role()/auth.jwt(). Compared daily against the LIVE database by scripts/ci/audit-live-definer-exposure.mjs. Anything not listed here is a finding. This list must only ever SHRINK: nineteen were closed on 2026-08-27 and two more on 2026-08-28, and each entry that remains was read line by line. get_current_settlement_period left on 2026-09-22: union_weekly_accounting_atomic_activation_20260917 retired both overloads to a refusal that writes nothing, and 20260920180734 revoked them from authenticated and service_role, so no browser role can reach either.

reviewedExceptions.recalculate_leaderboard_ranks: Recomputes dense_rank() over scores that are already in promotion_leaderboards for one promotion. It reads no input beyond the promotion id, writes no new value, moves no money, and is idempotent, so the worst an attacker achieves is the correct answer. Caller: src/services/PromotionService.ts:365, immediately after the RLS-gated score upsert.

reviewedTables.spatial_ref_sys: PostGIS's reference-system table: 8,500 rows of SRID definitions, in `public` with RLS disabled and arwdDxtm held by anon and authenticated. Confirmed reachable with the public anon key (GET returns rows, OPTIONS advertises POST), and it is not academic - find_live_games_nearby resolves coordinates through PostGIS, so corrupting SRID 4326 breaks venue search for everybody. IT CANNOT BE FIXED FROM HERE: the table is owned by supabase_admin and the grants were made BY supabase_admin, so postgres's REVOKE is a silent no-op and SET ROLE supabase_admin is denied 42501. Both were tried and both failed, on 2026-08-28. It needs an owner-level action through Supabase support or the dashboard. Baselined so a NEW RLS-off writable table still fails this audit loudly.

_comment_reviewedAnonReaders: QUESTION 4, added 2026-08-31. SECURITY DEFINER functions a LOGGED-OUT caller may execute that only READ and never consult auth.uid()/auth.role()/auth.jwt(). Questions 1-3 are all about writes, and on 2026-08-31 THREE read-only functions arrived anon-executable in one afternoon while this audit reported all clear: fn_tournament_metrics, fn_truly_unused_indexes and fn_nit_evictions. All three were closed. Unlike anon_writers this question needs a baseline, because a leaderboard and a name-availability check genuinely must answer somebody with no account - the finding is anything NEW. Each entry below says what an unauthenticated caller can actually learn. Two of them say more than their names suggest and are flagged for Dan; they are recorded here rather than quietly accepted.

reviewedAnonReaders.fn_shared_bonus_replay: A public bonus replay link, and the share uuid IS the capability. Reads one row of public.diamond_bonus_shares by id and returns its immutable payload: the game and prize snapshot that its authenticated owner explicitly shared after settlement. It returns no identity, wallet, club, entry id, seed or unshared game, holds no write capability, and answers {"ok":false,"error":"Replay Not Found"} for an id it does not hold, so it is not an enumeration oracle for anything a caller did not already possess. Reviewed and recorded twice already by migration 20260919153418_public_bonus_replay_has_an_explicitly_public_reader.sql - in public.ca_browser_definer_allowlist, which is what Telemetry Exposure reads, and in the anonPublicSurface block of scripts/ci/definer-authorization.allowlist.json, which is what the branch gate reads - but not here, which is the only list THIS audit reads. That third omission is what failed run 35799265680; tests/live-definer-exposure-audit.test.ts now refuses to let the two repository lists disagree again.
reviewedAnonReaders.fn_club_name_available: Takes a candidate club name and returns a boolean. It is the signup-time availability check and MUST answer before login, since a club is named while creating it. The only thing a caller learns is whether a name is taken, which the create form would tell them one submit later anyway. No id, no membership, no numbers.
reviewedAnonReaders.fn_global_leaderboard_period: The global leaderboard, which is a published ranking by design: the whole point is that anybody can look at it. Returns user_id plus the aggregate metric for the period, paginated. It exposes nothing that is not already on the public leaderboard page that renders it.
reviewedAnonReaders.fn_user_rank_global_period: One user's position in that same published global leaderboard, for a user_id the caller already has to know. It is the 'your rank' lookup beside the table above and discloses nothing the full leaderboard does not.
reviewedAnonReaders.get_public_profile_by_username: Public profile lookup by username: id, username, full_name, display_name, bio, avatar_url, level, created_at - the profile page a logged-out visitor is meant to see. FLAGGED FOR DAN 2026-08-31: it also returns `diamonds`, a balance-like number, to anyone who knows a username. That is a product decision about what a public profile shows, not a bug to fix inside a security sweep, so it is recorded here and raised rather than changed unilaterally.
reviewedAnonReaders.find_live_games_nearby: The public live-game finder: takes coordinates, a radius and optional game-type/stakes filters and returns venues running games. It is the map a visitor uses before signing up, and it reads venue and game data that is published on purpose. It resolves coordinates through PostGIS, which is why spatial_ref_sys above matters.
reviewedAnonReaders.find_similar_questions: Fuzzy-matches a question string against existing public Q&A entries so the ask form can offer duplicates before submitting. It reads only questions already published to the public help surface, and returns nothing that is not already listed there.
reviewedAnonReaders.fn_club_leaderboard_period_v2: One club's leaderboard for a period: per-member hands_played, total_winnings, total_losses, total_rake, tournaments_won and rank. It backs the club leaderboard tab. FLAGGED FOR DAN 2026-08-31: it takes ANY p_club_id and performs no membership check, so a caller with no account who knows a club's uuid can read that club's members' results. Club uuids are not enumerable, but they appear in invite links and URLs. Whether a club leaderboard is public, members-only, or a club setting is Dan's call about product behaviour, so it is recorded here and raised rather than changed unilaterally.
reviewedAnonReaders.fn_is_public_video_playback_eligible: A pure predicate over values the caller already holds (playback type, rights status, url, author, youtube id, canonical key). It returns whether that combination is publicly playable and reads no table, so an unauthenticated caller learns nothing it did not already supply. It backs 2 RLS policies on the public video surfaces, and a policy expression runs AS THE QUERYING ROLE - revoking anon here would deny every anonymous SELECT on those tables, which is the trap CLAUDE.md 10.84 records for fn_home_is_group_staff.
reviewedAnonReaders.fn_is_video_library_asset_eligible: Takes a video_library_videos id and answers whether that asset is publishable: a well-formed 11-character YouTube id, not a FAKE placeholder, and of a published type. An anon caller learns only what the public library page already shows them. Backs 1 RLS policy and must stay executable by anon for the same reason as above.
reviewedAnonReaders.fn_is_video_library_lineage_eligible: The same publish-eligibility question asked about an asset together with the identifiers a row claims for it, so a row cannot inherit playability from an asset it is not actually derived from. Reads only video_library_videos, returns a boolean, backs 2 RLS policies.
reviewedAnonReaders.legacy_transition_eligible: Two overloads, one on social_posts and one on social_reels, both pure row predicates: not deleted, publicly visible, playback_type youtube_embed, rights_status in embed_only/owned/licensed. Each answers exactly the question the public feed answers by rendering the item, and reads no table beyond the row it is handed. Each backs 2 RLS policies, and a policy expression is evaluated AS THE QUERYING ROLE - revoking anon would deny every anonymous SELECT on social_posts and social_reels. That is the trap CLAUDE.md 10.84 records for fn_home_is_group_staff, which is why these are baselined rather than revoked.
reviewedAnonReaders.fn_shared_bonus_replay: The public bonus replay link. Takes a share id and returns the frozen snapshot its owner chose to publish: game, diamonds, boost, completion time, payout chips and that game's settled outcome (Plinko drops, multipliers and risk table; Crash cashout and crash points; Mines and Donkey Cross picks, prizes and mine cells). Every id that was never shared gets the same {ok:false, Replay Not Found}. A share id is a random v4 uuid minted only by fn_diamond_bonus_share for the signed-in owner of a SETTLED bonus; the payload carries no user id, club id, bonus id, wallet balance or seed, and diamond_bonus_shares itself grants anon and authenticated nothing. It MUST answer before login: the link (https://smarter.poker/hub/club-arena/bonus-replay/<id>, which fn_diamond_bonus_share_to_feed also posts to the public feed) opens src/pages/share/SharedBonusReplayPage.tsx, routed as /bonus-replay/:shareId in the PUBLIC ROUTES block of src/App.tsx with no AuthGuard, which calls this through DiamondReplayService.read(shareId, true) in src/services/DiamondReplayService.ts. Read-only, backs no RLS policy. 20260919153418 (public_bonus_replay_has_an_explicitly_public_reader) recorded it as public in definer-authorization.allowlist.json and ca_browser_definer_allowlist but not here, so this audit failed on every run from 2026-09-19 17:25 UTC until this entry landed.
reviewedAnonReaders.fn_platform_capabilities: The platform capability registry, read by every client before it offers a product surface (Kill and Half-Kill, remaining variants and the rest), including on pages that render before login, so no control is shown that the database or engine cannot honour. Takes no argument and returns one entry per registered capability: its capability id, rule version, title, scope (platform, club, union, cash_table or tournament), supported variants, compatibility object, readiness state and the derived available flag (true only at deployed or production_verified). That is everything a caller with no account learns: which platform features exist and whether they are switched on, which the product shows to anyone who opens it. It returns no readiness evidence, no actor or event history, and no club, player, table or wallet data; the platform_capabilities table and platform_capability_events grant anon and authenticated nothing. Read-only: a single STABLE SQL SELECT that writes nothing; the only writer, fn_set_capability_readiness, admits service_role or platform staff and is not anon-executable.
